title: Multi-task PLR with ordinal (CORAL) rating auxiliary loss: does forcing the shared representation to encode rating<->satisfaction coupling break the redundancy frontier? (catalogue items 35+36)
motivation: Every candidate measured so far lands on a hard frontier: decorrelated (corr ~0.76-0.989) but too weak (standalone 0.925-0.957), or strong (~0.960) but redundant (corr ~0.993-0.997). All of them predict satisfaction ALONE. Multi-task learning changes WHAT is learned, not just the architecture: an auxiliary head that must reconstruct each masked service rating from the other features (incl. the satisfaction-correlated structure) forces the shared representation to model the 13-rating coupling graph, which the boosted-tree aux arms only capture through split geometry. Item 36 adds the ordinal (CORAL cumulative) loss, which respects the 0..5 ordering that MSE/CE would discard. This is supervised end-to-end MTL and is NOT the closed SSL32 branch (unsupervised masked-reconstruction PRETRAINING followed by supervised fine-tuning -- different mechanism, recorded as such).
why_masking: The 13 ratings are INPUT features. An auxiliary head trained on unmasked inputs can be minimized by copying rating values through idle trunk dimensions: zero representation pressure, a guaranteed-negative control. Per-(sample,rating) input masking (set to the standardized mean) makes the aux task genuinely inferential.

scope.cannot: pass the OOF admission gate; justify a submission; or establish private performance
scope.purpose: decide whether masked multi-task learning merits a full 5-fold OOF + admission-gate run

protocol.feature_representation: certified rich view 'full' (285 features) via ViewBuilder.assemble; ratings are view columns 0..12 (asserted)
protocol.target_encoding: fold-safe TE only (inner cross-fit on FIT; EVAL labels never read)
protocol.training: AdamW, warmup 5 + cosine, inner 10% ES split carved from FIT ONLY, judged on satisfaction AUC under INFERENCE conditions (no masking)
protocol.aux_targets: the 13 raw service ratings of the SAME row (observed inputs, not labels -- no label involved beyond the satisfaction target)
protocol.arch: MultiTaskPLR: PLR periodic embedding -> 2-layer MLP trunk -> 128-d shared -> main head + CORAL aux head (13 ratings x 5 thresholds)
protocol.amendment: arch_kwargs/train_kwargs added after the runner hit KeyError on the prose-only spec; amended and re-hashed BEFORE any MTL prediction existed (both invocations failed at config load, zero GPU-seconds of training)
protocol.reference: plrmlp_full_fold0 (same trunk family, no MTL): AUC 0.9601974099474075, port_delta -4.191e-4, corr 0.9937

metrics.paired_reference: plrmlp_full_fold0 -- the single-factor ablation (same trunk family, p_mask=0, lam=0)

decision_rule.MECHANISM_INACTIVE: if both arms land within +-1e-4 of the plrmlp reference on standalone AUC and +-0.005 on corr, the MTL objective is representation-inactive for this view; close items 35/36 as measured
decision_rule.NEGATIVE: otherwise (both arms below bar): MTL-with-ordinal-aux closes; reopening requires a different auxiliary signal, not another (p_mask, lam) sweep
decision_rule.note: PROMISING only means 'run full 5-fold OOF + admission gate'.

anti_leakage: Aux targets are observed input columns (ratings), not labels; no competition label beyond satisfaction is read.
Training uses FIT only; inner ES carved from FIT; the eval fold is never touched by loss, scaler, or masking.
TE features are fold-safe (inner cross-fit on FIT; EVAL encoded by a FIT-fitted table).
Champion reference hash-asserted from phase17_B1 artifacts.

budget.gpu: ~1-3 min per arm on the RTX 5070 Ti (PLR full-view reference trained in 18s; MTL adds one aux head + masking)

predeclared_followups: A control arm (p_mask=0, lam=0 = plain PLR) already exists as plrmlp_full_fold0 and is NOT rerun.
No (p_mask, lam) grid search: two arms max, decided in advance.
